_doc: Maps the single Z-Anatomy body (sources/z-anatomy Startup.blend) to our 7 systems + skin. Authored from a headless dump of collection contents (see scripts/extract_core.py). Everything is extracted from ONE body with ONE normalize transform, so alignment is guaranteed by construction. Budgets here are spike-level (offline coherence render); paring to the app's 150k total is a later curation pass.
_drop_suffixes_doc: .l/.r are left/right (kept). .j/.i are 2-vertex landmark/junction helpers; .g are label-group anchors. All have 0 tris.
_repro_doc: No reproductive system in our 7, and genitalia are inappropriate for a clinic kiosk. Dropped everywhere.
_artifact_doc: Construction/handle-broken curves in the atlas that tessellate to wild multi-meter extents. Dropped everywhere; a generous outlier-vertex clip in extract_core.py is the backstop for any others.
_nc_doc: Inner ear (Dundee, CC-BY-NC-SA) must be excluded for commercial use. Lives in the nervous/sense-organ collection.

urinary._license_flag_doc: Z-Anatomy kidney provenance is ambiguous (Lissie Cowley CC-BY-NC vs BodyParts3D CC-BY-SA). Included for the spike; verify/swap to a CC-BY-SA kidney before commercial use.

_visceral_priority_doc: Collection 8 holds 4 systems mixed. Each object is assigned to the FIRST system whose include list matches, in this order. Endocrine before urinary so 'suprarenal' wins over the 'renal' substring.

skin._doc: 299 surface-region patches that tile the whole body. Joined (minus hairs) = a frosted skin envelope co-registered with the organs. Patchwork topology (no single mesh) — fine as a shell, but see the skin/morph spike re: whether it can take outward body-type morphs.
